record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal evaluations of released models after a directional-ablation weight edit. This tests practical removal, but Heretic uses an optimized, parameterized variant rather than the original causal activation-ablation procedure.
record.gate_note: The README table reports refusal rates and KL divergence for the original Gemma model and three abliterated checkpoints; these are recorded below. The residual-geometry table is presented as an example output of a research feature, but it does not report a causal intervention or refusal outcome, so it is not entered as a result row.
record.test_reason: The README table gives refusal counts on 100 harmful prompts for Gemma-3-12B-it before (97/100) and after three directional-ablation weight edits (3/100 each). That bears directly on V2. It is a parameterized, optimizer-tuned variant of abliteration, not the original activation-ablation procedure.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The README says Heretic, run unsupervised with default settings, matches manual abliterations' refusal suppression (3/100) at much lower KL divergence. It reads the lower KL as less capability damage, but supports that only with the KL proxy and user anecdotes.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a parameterized directional-ablation weight edit: it computes per-layer harmful-minus-harmless first-token residual means and orthogonalizes selected projection matrices. It adds flexible layer/component weights and automatic TPE optimization; it does not report the original activation-projection ablation procedure or a direct addition test. This is a tool repository.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says results can depend on platform and hardware; exact values may vary. It also describes layer/component-specific weights and direction selection as optimizable parameters, but reports no separate outcome rows for those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On harmless prompts, KL divergence from the original is 1.04 (mlabonne), 0.45 (huihui-ai) and 0.16 (Heretic) at equal refusal suppression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizing the per-layer and per-component ablation weights reduces distribution shift on harmless prompts at equal refusal removal. KL alone does not establish preserved capability.

record.problems: The reported comparison is a README-reported evaluation without uncertainty estimates or a direct general-capability benchmark; the README notes that exact values may vary by platform and hardware. It also states that mathematical metrics and automated benchmarks do not replace human evaluation.
record.rows_left_out: No additional README-reported behavioral evaluation rows were present. The residual-geometry example is not an intervention or behavioral result, so it was not entered as a row.

untested.parts: Only one model family (Gemma-3-12B-it) is evaluated quantitatively. No capability benchmarks, no uncertainty, and the refusal judge is unstated. Other models (GPT-OSS 20B, Qwen3-4B) are backed only by user anecdotes.
No activation ablation or addition test and no capability retention test. The table shows weight-edit outcomes only.
The interpolated direction index is said to 'often' find better directions than any single layer, but no numbers are given.
GPT-OSS 20B Heretic is mentioned only through user quotes. No refusal measurement.

record.verdict_notes: This repository (doriangallo/heretic-local, created 2026, 4 stars) reproduces p-e-w/heretic's README verbatim, citation and copyright included. The table is p-e-w's result, so treat this as a likely duplicate of the p-e-w/heretic source to avoid double counting. Rows are README claims, compiled on one RTX 5090 setup, with values the README says are hardware-dependent. The residual-geometry table (gemma-3-270m) is descriptive only and correctly left out. The 'MLP interventions more damaging than attention' remark is unquantified.

versions.untested_parts: No direct residual-stream ablation or addition test, and no behavioral test of whether other abilities remain intact.
The README reports refusal evaluation for one Heretic-generated model and two other abliterated models, not a systematic evaluation across released models.
No test of jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
The example geometry output does not test whether refusal is carried by an affine set, cone, or multiple directions.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No transfer test across languages, model variants, or base and instruct stages.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages.
